mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has fallen in three consecutive weeks from -31.0 to -46.1, showing strong negative momentum. Persistent activity suppression tends to be autocorrelated, so the trend should continue, producing a lower mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days than the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined from -31.0 to -46.1 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28 days despite the observed three-week downward run.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week drop in TRANSIT usage typically reflects newly imposed or tightened mobility restrictions that reduce discretionary travel to retail and recreation venues within one to two weeks of the transit decline.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -37.3 to -47.4 between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall further over the next 2 weeks despite TRANSIT dropping more than 10 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in RESIDENTIAL time and decline in WORKPLACES mobility indicates households are compounding stay-at-home behavior, which jointly suppresses retail and recreation trips more than either series would alone, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises and WORKPLACES falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 9.7 to 14.3 while WORKPLACES fell from -24.0 to -29.4 over the same four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 4 weeks even though RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES continue to move in the compounding direction.

mechanism_narrative: A collapse in PARKS mobility after a prior spike signals that outdoor recreation is no longer substituting for indoor retail activity, which under an active restriction regime accelerates near-term declines in RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 0 after a prior positive reading
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 29.7 at t-2w to -2.3 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week following a PARKS reversal from positive to negative territory.

mechanism_narrative: Stable GROCERY_PHARM mobility near baseline despite falling RETAIL_REC suggests essential-trip demand has floored out while discretionary retail is oversold relative to seasonal norms, implying a mean-reverting uptick in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as autumn indoor shopping resumes.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed within -6 to -9 while RETAIL_REC fell to -46.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days remains lower than the last 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM staying flat near baseline.

mechanism_narrative: As PARKS mobility crosses from positive to negative with the onset of cooler autumn weather, outdoor recreation substitutes shift back toward indoor retail and recreation venues, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 0 for the first time after a sustained positive period
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS was positive at t-3w and t-2w (4.4, 29.7) then turned negative at t-1w (-2.3)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to fall for two weeks after PARKS crosses below zero, indicating no seasonal substitution effect.

evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -37.3 to -50.0 and WORKPLACES fell from -22.1 to -29.4 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next 2 weeks despite simultaneous declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 9.7 to 14.3 over the last four weeks, remaining elevated above 9 percent throughout
